gen-silkscreen-gf-koho: Silkscreen spaces every letter out like spaghetti laid flat, its marker-nib line ignoring direction altogether, retro and lo-fi. KoHo steps in below with wide apertures, tidy and plain.
gen-silkscreen-gf-kosugi: Retro and lo-fi, Silkscreen scatters letters like spaghetti with space around each one. Kosugi sits below as sans-serif text with an open-jawed c, wire-bent and clean, so the display heading and body each keep their own job.
gen-silkscreen-gf-kulim-park: Loose, lo-fi spaghetti letters: Silkscreen floats each one in its own space, then hands off to Kulim Park. Kulim Park's open e and clean-ended terminals keep text friendly.
gen-silkscreen-gf-kumbh-sans: Silkscreen lays its lo-fi, retro letters out like spaghetti, each one surrounded by space you can almost feel. But the pair's real strength is the gap between display play and Kumbh Sans, drawn with a fixed pen.
gen-silkscreen-gf-lato: Lato reads clean, with wide s curves barely curled in. Beneath Silkscreen's marker-traced, retro lettering with its spaced-out spaghetti look, paragraphs of Lato would run smooth and quietly unfussy.
gen-silkscreen-gf-libre-franklin: Lo-fi at heart, Silkscreen gives every o a ring-like constant wall and lets each letter float in its own space. Silkscreen shows off; Libre Franklin, plain sans, does the reading.
gen-silkscreen-gf-livvic: Spaghetti letters, lo-fi and retro, each in its own space. Livvic, a plain sans with unstressed curves and a generous c, gives Silkscreen's display play a friendly, clean counterpart.
gen-silkscreen-gf-lunasima: Silkscreen is lo-fi and retro, with spaced-out letters like spaghetti and terminals that finish at the width they started. And Lunasima, clean and contemporary with c tips held well apart, gives it a tidy sans-serif partner.
gen-silkscreen-gf-lxgw-marker-gothic: Spaghetti letters, loose, lo-fi and retro. Silkscreen looks bent from a single wire, while LXGW Marker Gothic, a contemporary sans-serif, lets its stems outweigh hairlines only slightly, with a wide-open c.
gen-silkscreen-gf-m-plus-1: Lo-fi spaghetti letters define Silkscreen, each with space around it you can almost feel. And M PLUS 1, with big open eyes on e and a and fineliner-flat lines, is what makes the pairing click.
